chunks: And by this chain, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is one who is relieved and one from whom relief is sought. As for the one who is relieved, it is the righteous servant who is relieved from the sorrow of the world and what was in it of worship [striving] to the rest and bliss of the Hereafter. And as for the one from whom relief is sought, it is the evil-doer from whom are relieved the two Angels who record [his deeds], and his servant, and his family, and the ground upon which he used to walk.'

key_terms.مُسْتَرَاحٌ مِنْهُ: The one from whom relief is sought (by others)
key_terms.مُسْتَرِيحٌ: The one who is relieved (from burdens)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the righteous servant and the evil-doer in terms of relief after death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the dual nature of posthumous relief, contrasting the righteous believer who finds peace in the Hereafter with the wicked whose departure brings ease to the cosmic order. It reflects the Shia understanding of the physical and spiritual universe as responsive to human moral states, where even the earth and angels experience relief from the presence of the unjust.
